description:
The number that turns a count into a decision: how many of this threat, on this crop, at this growth stage, before somebody has to act. It is a RECORD rather than a constant in code because the number is local — an extension bulletin for the Hood River valley and one for Yakima do not agree, and a farm that has watched its own blocks for ten years disagrees with both. A threshold nobody can edit is one a crew quietly stops believing.

THE COMPARISON IS A COLUMN, not an assumption. Most thresholds are 'act above this', but a nutrient threshold is 'act BELOW this' — tissue nitrogen under 2.2 percent is the finding, not over. Hard-coding greater-than would have made half the six threat categories unrepresentable, and the half it broke would be the half that fails silently: a nutrient threshold of 2.2 with a greater-than rule fires on every healthy block and never on a deficient one.

CROP STAGE IS OPTIONAL AND MATCHES WIDEST-LAST. A blank stage is the fallback for the season; a stage-specific row beats it. Codling moth at 2 per trap means something different at petal fall than at first cover, and a single season-long number is the one both camps will argue was wrong.

fields.description: The crop this threshold is for — 'Cherry', 'Apple', 'Pear'. Free text rather than a link, matched case-insensitively, for the same reason Field.crop is: a block of table grapes should not be a schema change.
fields.label: Crop

fields.description: Which of the six kinds of threat this is. The categories are fixed because they are what an IPM programme reports against, and a seventh invented on one farm would drop out of every roll-up.
fields.label: Threat Category
fields.options:
Insect
Disease
Weed
Vertebrate
Abiotic
Nutrient

fields.description: The specific threat — 'Codling Moth', 'Powdery Mildew', 'Vole', 'Boron'. Matched case-insensitively against what a scout types.
fields.label: Threat

fields.description: The growth stage this number applies at — 'Petal Fall', 'First Cover', a BBCH code. BLANK MEANS EVERY STAGE and is the fallback: a stage-specific row beats it, and where none matches, the blank one is used.
fields.label: Crop Stage

fields.description: What the number counts. A threshold and an observation that disagree about the unit are two numbers nobody should compare — 'two per trap' against 'two percent infested' is the kind of mistake that reads as fine.
fields.label: Sample Unit
fields.options:
Per Trap
Per Trap Per Week
Per Leaf
Per Shoot
Per Branch
Per Tree
Per 100 Fruit
Per Sq Ft
Percent Infested
Percent Defoliation
Degree Days
Percent Dry Weight
PPM
Count

fields.description: When this number takes effect. A threshold revised mid-season does not retroactively change what last month's scouting decided.
fields.label: Effective From

fields.description: Retired rather than deleted, so the recommendations it generated still resolve to the number that generated them.
fields.label: Disabled

fields.description: Which direction counts as exceeding. 'Greater Than' for a pest count; 'Less Than' for a nutrient or a soil moisture floor, where the finding is that the number has fallen too far. This is a column and not an assumption — see the doctype description for what hard-coding it would have broken.
fields.label: Comparison
fields.options:
Greater Than
Greater Than Or Equal
Less Than
Less Than Or Equal

fields.description: Cross this and an IPM recommendation is generated. The number a crew acts on.
fields.label: Action Threshold

fields.description: Optional early number. Crossing it raises the pest's pressure to Watch without generating a recommendation — a farm gets a week's notice rather than an alarm on the morning it is already too late. Must sit on the safe side of the action threshold, in whichever direction the comparison runs.
fields.label: Warning Threshold

fields.description: Predator-to-pest ratio above which no action is recommended even though the count is over threshold. THIS IS THE WHOLE OF IPM IN ONE COLUMN: a mite count over threshold with a healthy population of predatory mites eating it is a block that is already handling itself, and spraying it kills the predators and guarantees the second flare. Leave blank where no beneficial is being counted.
fields.label: Beneficial Ratio Minimum

fields.description: How many units have to be examined before a count off this threshold means anything. Two infested leaves out of five is not twenty percent infestation; it is a sample too small to say. An observation under this size is flagged rather than acted on.
fields.label: Minimum Sample Size

fields.description: What to do when it is crossed, one action per line, each optionally prefixed with a control method and a colon — 'Biological: release predatory mites', 'Cultural: remove alternate hosts on the headland', 'Chemical: cover spray at label rate'. These seed the generated recommendation's actions, which is what makes the threshold engine produce something a person can act on rather than an alarm.
fields.label: Recommended Methods

fields.description: Where the number came from — an extension bulletin, a certifier's standard, or the farm's own record. A threshold with no provenance is one nobody will defend when it is inconvenient.
fields.label: Source
Organism
fields.description: The IPM graph node this threshold is for. The phone's threshold status and the graph read it.

fields.label: Status
fields.description: Seeded starter thresholds and AI proposals are Proposed and disabled until a person approves them (approve_pest_action_threshold).

fields.label: Provenance
fields.options:
User Entered
Literature
Farm Observed
AI Proposed
